title: DeNOTS: Stable Deep Neural ODEs for Time Series
claim: Deepening a model by lowering tolerance barely helps, while scaling the time horizon with stabilized dynamics keeps improving accuracy and the unstabilized variants collapse.
layout: single line plot with top legend, scatter points behind smoothed curves
description: A single line chart with a two-row, four-column legend above it. The x-axis shows log-NFEs, from about 4.2 to 5.4. The y-axis shows metric R², from 0.50 to 0.85. Faint scatter points sit behind the smoothed curves. Four colored solid curves show the time-scale variants: Tanh-S in blue, No NF-S in orange, Sync-NF-S in green and Anti-NF-S (ours) in red. The blue and orange curves peak early and then fall steeply as NFEs grow. The green curve rises and flattens near 0.77. The red curve climbs steadily to about 0.81 and ends highest. Four gray curves, in dashed, dash-dot, solid and dotted styles, show the tolerance-lowering variants. They stay flat at around 0.62 to 0.69. The eye goes first to the red curve rising above the gray cluster.
caption: $R^2$ vs Log-NFEs on the Pendulum dataset for various methods of increasing NFEs: -T for lowering tolerance, -S for increasing time scale; for various vector fields (VF): Tanh --- MLP with $\tanh$ activation; No NF --- vanilla GRU VF, Sync NF --- GRU-ODE VF, Anti NF --- our version. The curves were drawn via Radial Basis Function interpolation.
abstract: Neural CDEs provide a natural way to process the temporal evolution of irregular time series. The number of function evaluations (NFE) is these systems' natural analog of depth (the number of layers in traditional neural networks). It is usually regulated via solver error tolerance: lower tolerance means higher numerical precision, requiring more integration steps. However, lowering tolerances does not adequately increase the models' expressiveness. We propose a simple yet effective alternative: scaling the integration time horizon to increase NFEs and "deepen`` the model. Increasing the integration interval causes uncontrollable growth in conventional vector fields, so we also propose a way to stabilize the dynamics via Negative Feedback (NF). It ensures provable stability without constraining flexibility. It also implies robustness: we provide theoretical bounds for Neural ODE risk using Gaussian process theory. Experiments on four open datasets demonstrate that our method, DeNOTS, outperforms existing approaches~ -- ~including recent Neural RDEs and state space models,~ -- ~achieving up to $20\%$ improvement in metrics. DeNOTS combines expressiveness, stability, and robustness, enabling reliable modelling in continuous-time domains.
